title: Gate and Fence Breach Sequence Correlation
dataSources: Object detections (`frigate:event`), camera health (`camera:health`), alarm state changes (`alarm:event`), smart-lock access (`lock:access`), plate and gate events (`gate:event`), and doorbell delivery telemetry (`doorbell:event`).
app: Home-security telemetry from Frigate and Blue Iris detections, camera health feeds, smart locks, alarm panels, doorbells, and gate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and Home Assistant integrations.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=gate:event
| sort 0 _time
| streamstats window=1 current=f last(sensor) as prev_sensor last(_time) as prev_time by zone
| eval correlated=if(prev_sensor="fence" AND sensor="gate" AND _time-prev_time<=120,1,0)
| stats sum(correlated) as breach_sequences by zone
description: Correlates fence-trigger and gate-trigger events that happen close together to identify likely perimeter entries rather than isolated noise.
value: Multi-sensor sequences reduce false alarms and give you a clearer view of when something actually crossed the perimeter.
implementation: Normalize gate magnetic contacts and fence sensors to a shared zone name, then look for short event chains.
visualization: Table of likely breach sequences by perimeter zone.
grandmaExplanation: It watches when two nearby security sensors trip in a pattern that looks more like a real entry than random movement.
